title: Use the Beads change journal for incremental refreshes
objective: Reduce repeated full issue reads using the opt-in Beads 1.3 CLI events journal, retaining compatibility with older installations and rebuilding current state when the journal cannot safely represent it. This intent is a prerequisite for the implementation of GitHub issue #15.
acceptance_criteria: After an initial full snapshot, automatic refreshes use bd events tail --since with independent in-memory checkpoints for each configured project when its journal is enabled; Beadle does not enable the journal or start an HTTP server.
Baseline checkpoint acquisition precedes the full snapshot read so writes during initialization cannot be skipped; advance a checkpoint only after successfully applying the complete batch.

Apply create, update, close, delete, dependency and comment events without stale issue detail caches. Preserve correct relationship and count information when event snapshots omit it, using targeted reads or a full rebuild where necessary.
Interpret missing is_blocked as false and preserve closed and in-progress status semantics while reflecting dependency-driven blocked state.

Older CLIs, disabled journals, truncated checkpoints, invalid records and read failures safely fall back to current-state snapshots; failed loads retain cached results and expose the existing project error behavior.

Discard checkpoints when projects or the configured executable change. Manual refresh rebuilds from current state, and a documented bounded reconciliation interval catches unjournaled pulls, branch changes, journal resets and direct writes.
Tests exercise baseline races, independent cursors, replay and deletion, blocked transitions, incomplete event snapshots, fallback and truncation, checkpoint resets and reconciliation.
README explains the opt-in command, compatibility fallback, refresh and reconciliation behavior. HTTP preview integration is outside this change.
maquina contract validate, maquina policy check, swift build, swift test and git diff --check pass.
